knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Secant

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{3}{|x|\sqrt{9 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=3 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

The substitution factor is positive, so the absolute values satisfy

$$
|u|=|3 x|=3|x|,\qquad \frac{1}{|x|}=\frac{3}{|u|}.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{3}{|x|\sqrt{9 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9\int \frac{1}{|3 x|\sqrt{(3 x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9(\frac{1}{3})\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 3\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 3 \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 3 \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(3 x \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

This antiderivative applies on either interval where $|3 x|>1$; the constant may differ between those intervals.

question.:question/problem:

\int \frac{1}{2|x|\sqrt{4 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.

\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{2|x|\sqrt{4 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{|2 x|\sqrt{(2 x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1(\frac{1}{2})\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}}{2}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(2 x \right)}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
